name_note: GTDB calls this species Roseburia rectalis; its genomes carry the NCBI name Agathobacter rectalis and most papers call it Eubacterium rectale.

sentences.text: Eubacterium rectale, as the species is usually called in the literature, is one of the most prevalent bacteria of the human gut.
More than 1300 genomes reconstructed from over 6500 metagenomes show geographic stratification, including a subspecies found predominantly in African individuals.
It is an acetate-converting butyrate producer and cross-feeds with Bifidobacterium longum growing on arabinoxylan oligosaccharides.
With Roseburia relatives it forms a dominant group of butyrate producers, averaging about seven percent of faecal bacteria detected in ten healthy volunteers.
